directorialGrammar.progressiveRevealRule: Never show all joke elements at the beginning of a sentence. Elements enter strictly in chronological order matching spoken keywords.
directorialGrammar.snapZoomChoreography: Use hard snap cuts and dynamic punch-ins (< 150ms) for punchlines, escalating absurdity, and forensic examinations. Zero slow 5-second dragging pans.
directorialGrammar.sub100msAudioSync: All asset entrances, stamp slams, zooms, and facial expressions land within +/- 100ms of spoken audio cues.

characterActing.speechFlap: Vertical mouth flap Math.sin(timeSec * 16) during speech
characterActing.punchlineExpressions: Extreme reactions (shock_eye_pop, mind_blown_galaxy_brain, cringe_teeth_grit, fear_sweat_freeze) held for 1.0-2.0s at climax before resolving to deadpan

scenes.name: The Beauty Standard Pendulum & Slouching Couch Guy

scenes.name: 90s Heroin Chic, Food Pyramid & Victorian Disease
scenes.transcript: If we rewind to the 90s and early 2000s, we had an era affectionately dubbed “Heroin Chick.” This was pioneered by models like Kate Moss, and the overarching goal was to look like you sustained yourself entirely on Diet Coke, Parliament cigarettes, and pure, unfiltered apathy. You were supposed to look like you were perpetually recovering from a minor Victorian wasting disease, but in a cool, fashionable way.

scenes.name: 2010s BBL & Pixar Mom Gravitational Field
scenes.transcript: Then, as the 2010s rolled around, the pendulum swung violently in the opposite direction. We entered the era of the BBL, or Brazilian Butt Lift, where the ideal body type shifted to what biologists might classify as “Pixar Mom.” Celebrities were suddenly buying curves, and the internet was flooded with fitness influencers who insisted their new, localized gravitational pull was entirely due to doing a lot of squats, despite the fact that their calves and forearms remained the exact same size.

scenes.name: Overfilled Hourglass & Corporate PR Body Positivity
scenes.transcript: For about ten years, the ultimate flex was looking like an hourglass that had been overfilled at the bottom. During this exact same time, society also pushed heavily for “body positivity.” We were told by countless brands and PR agencies that all bodies are beautiful, that you don’t have to be a size zero to be a leading lady, and that Hollywood was finally progressing past its shallow, aesthetic-obsessed roots.

scenes.name: Fidget Spinner, Podcast & Boss Closes Tab
scenes.transcript: Well, it turns out, body positivity was less of a permanent cultural shift and more of a temporary trend—kind of like fidget spinners, or pretending to care about your friend’s podcast. As soon as a pharmaceutical shortcut dropped that allowed rich people to just opt out of their natural body weight, the industry abandoned the “every body is beautiful” narrative with the swiftness of someone closing a browser tab when their boss walks by.

scenes.name: Y2K Organ-Hostile Fashion & Miu Miu Micro-Belt
scenes.transcript: Because right alongside the medical advancements, the fashion industry decided it was time to bring back Y2K fashion. And for those of you who don’t know, Y2K fashion is incredibly hostile to anyone who possesses internal organs. We are talking about low-rise jeans that sit below the pelvic bone, baby tees that offer the coverage of a moderately sized napkin, and the infamous Miu Miu micro-skirt, which is essentially just a belt that costs two thousand dollars. You physically cannot participate in this trend if you have a functioning digestive tract that occasionally needs to process solid food.
